q: `async function f() { return 200; }` What does f() return?
a: A Promise<number> (fulfilled with 200). An async function ALWAYS returns a Promise. Use await f() to get 200.

q: Name 3 symptoms of a forgotten await.
a: 1) Property 'x' does not exist on type 'Promise<...>' / Received: Promise {}. 2) The check runs before the value is ready. 3) The test passes for the wrong reason (a Promise is truthy), or the error shows up in another test / 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'.

q: Which need await: page.goto(), page.getByRole(), locator.click(), expect(locator).toBeVisible(), expect(5).toBe(5)?
a: await: page.goto(), locator.click(), expect(locator).toBeVisible(). NO await: page.getByRole() (a locator is just a description) and expect(5).toBe(5) (a plain value).

q: Why is `items.forEach(async (item) => { await ... })` a bug?
a: forEach does not wait for async callbacks: it starts them all and moves on. Use for...of with await, or Promise.all(items.map(...)).

q: When must async steps be sequential, and when can you use Promise.all?
a: Sequential when a step needs the result of the previous one (login -> token -> cart) or order matters. Promise.all when they are independent.

q: Error: "'await' expressions are only allowed within async functions and at the top levels of modules." Fix?
a: Add async to the function that contains the await: async function f() {...} or async () => {...}.

q: Error: "locator.click: Target page, context or browser has been closed". Most likely cause?
a: A missing await: the test ended (and the browser closed) before the action ran. Add await before the action.

q: Inside try { return fetchUser(id); } catch { return null; } the catch never runs on errors. Why?
a: The promise is returned, not awaited, so it rejects after the try is over. Write return await fetchUser(id); to wait inside the try.

q: Why should real Playwright tests avoid page.waitForTimeout(2000) / sleep?
a: It always waits the full time (slow) and can still be too short (flaky). Web-first assertions like await expect(locator).toBeVisible() wait exactly as long as needed.
